text: Which of the following correctly states the completeness theorem for propositional logic?
choices: Every formula is either a tautology or a contradiction
If a formula is a tautology, there exists a proof of it in any complete proof system
If a formula is a tautology, then it is derivable in natural deduction
A formula is satisfiable if and only if it has a proof
explanation: Completeness for propositional logic states: if a formula φ is a tautology (true in every truth-value assignment), then φ is derivable (provable) in the proof system. Together with soundness (all derivable formulas are tautologies), this gives: ⊨φ ↔ ⊢φ. Option C correctly captures this direction. Option B is also nearly correct but any complete proof system is circular. Option D conflates satisfiability with provability.
